Additive manufacturing (AM) has been increasingly adopted by gas turbine manufacturers for rapid prototyping and mass production of complex, lightweight parts for combustion systems.
The AM process typically results in higher surface roughness compared to conventional manufacturing.
Surface roughness effects are difficult to model efficiently with high accuracy, leading to performance differences between design concepts and as-built parts.
The new integral wall model for LES (iWLES) uses a velocity profile with a viscous/roughness sublayer and a logarithmic layer to capture near-wall physics.
The iWLES model was implemented as a user-defined function in the ANSYS Fluent software.
The iWLES model was validated on a periodic channel flow case and a flat plate boundary layer case with distributed surface roughness.

Applying the improvements enabled by accurate surface roughness modeling to a fleet of 5,000 turbofan engines could result in $6B in annual fuel cost savings and 25 million tons per year reduction in CO2 emissions.
